transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-03-12 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Evan Chen (Redwood SE), Marisol Ruiz (Aurora Head of ML), James O'Neal (Aurora Platform), Priya Singh (Aurora CTO)

Summary (auto):
Quick scoping for a POC focused on benchmark planning and harness integration. Discussed success criteria (p95 latency, throughput, error budget), workload sizing, customer scripts, load test windows, and streaming vs non-streaming approaches. Agreed to exchange harness and sample payloads; schedule coordinated load test.

Topics: benchmark harness, customer scripts, load testing, streaming vs non-streaming, success criteria, timelines

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — i'm Sofia, AE on the Redwood team, and Evan our SE is with me. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Marisol: good, thanks. i'm Marisol. we lead ML at Aurora. Priya and James are on the call too.
[00:20] Priya: hi all. quick schedule note — we only have the 54 minutes so hoping to cover test plan and next steps.
[00:28] Evan: cool. i'll start with what our benchmark harness looks like, high level, and then we can map to your scripts. there might be a few mispronounced things in the transcript, sorry in advance — audio's a little echoey.
[00:40] Evan: the harness is a small go/python service that runs orchestrated requests against the endpoint. supports streaming and non-streaming modes, can replay your recorded request traces, and has paramizable concurrency and sequence-length distributions. we provide a docker image and a repo: github.com/redwood/benchmark-harness (link).
[01:05] James: when you say streaming do you mean server-sent events style or chunked HTTP? we use a gRPC streaming gateway in front of our app.
[01:14] Evan: good q. currently the harness supports chunked HTTP streaming for token-by-token streaming and a separate gRPC client in the repo that can be enabled. both produce slightly different latencies — streaming reduces perceived latency for the first tokens, but can increase server-side overhead.
[01:36] Marisol: our main POC workload is clinical note summarization, batched -- sequences vary 512 to 3k tokens, typical is around 1.2k. throughput target would be ~50 concurrent requests, p95 latency under 1.2s for summaries, and cost per 1k requests within an agreed band.
[02:02] Evan: noted. that token range is helpful. for sizing we'll need sample payloads representative of those lengths, and a distribution file if possible. if you don't have a distribution upfront, we can start with synthetic mixtures.
[02:20] Priya: security question — how does the harness talk to your hosted endpoints? we need SSO + KMS for keys and also audit logs.
[02:29] Sofia: good callout. for the POC we can run the harness from your VPC into Redwood Private, or we can run it from our hosted lab. if you run from your VPC we hand over a service account and you keep keys in your KMS. audit logs are available and we'll share the SOC2 docs. we'll attach the security whitepaper in the follow-ups.
[02:52] James: perfect. technical — will you be able to replay our exact client-side pre- and post-processing? we do a small tokenization tweak and post-filtering at the platform layer.
[03:01] Evan: yeah we recommend bringing your real repo hooks as a shim — the harness accepts a pre/post-processing hook configurable in the runner. we can pair on integration. sometimes tokenization differences show up in latency since longer tokenization increases input length.
[03:25] Marisol: for success criteria, beyond p95 latency, we want correctness held to the same automated eval baseline (ROUGE or clinical-bleu-ish) — if quantization or batching reduces quality we need regression alerts.
[03:37] Evan: totally. our POC template ties generation metrics to your eval harness. we can run inference side-by-side with a baseline model and track per-prompt diffs. we can also run A/B with Canary routing.
[03:55] Priya: timeline — how long to set up and run the first load test? we ideally want results within 2 weeks.
[04:03] Sofia: realistic schedule: day 0-3 exchange artifacts (scripts, S3 sample), day 4-7 integration & dry runs, week 2 run full load windows and collect metrics, week 3 analysis and tune. so 10–14 business days is doable if artifacts come promptly.
[04:25] James: we can probably upload sample payloads by Tue 2025-03-18.
[04:30] Sofia: great. we'll target load windows week of 2025-03-24 and allocate a 3-hour run with varying concurrency.
[04:40] Evan: a few notes on test matrix — we'll do: non-streaming baseline (sync HTTP), streaming token-chunked, varying batch sizes (1, 4, 8), and KV cache warm vs cold. also repeat runs across model variants (fp16, 4-bit quant).
[05:03] Marisol: KV cache — i keep hearing K-V cash in the auto-notes — that's the KV cache for generation right?
[05:08] Evan: yes, KV cache (key-value cache) — sorry the transcript might show K-V cash. it's the attention cache used by decoder models; warming it drastically drops p95 for multi-turn chat but matters less for single-turn summarization.
[05:25] Priya: on throughput measurement — are you measuring tokens/sec or requests/sec? we need both because our billing ties to token count.
[05:34] Evan: we measure both; the harness emits per-request token counts, latency histogram (p50/p90/p95/p99), error rates, and resource metrics (GPU utilization, memory, and kernel stalls). we'll provide a CSV + Grafana dashboard snapshot.
[05:55] Sofia: small practical: we recommend replaying a week's worth of traffic in the test window but throttled so you can observe tail latency at scale. that often surfaces N+1 issues.
[06:10] James: what about client-level timeouts? our gateway has a 10s timeout. if streaming is used first-token latency matters.
[06:18] Evan: we'll include per-endpoint timeout checks and can measure first-byte time separately. for streaming we also capture per-chunk latency distribution.
[06:30] Marisol: do you support warm/cold start tests for Dedicated nodes? we're evaluating Redwood Dedicated as an option.
[06:38] Evan: yes — we can spin up Dedicated-equivalent nodes in the lab or run tests in your Dedicated instance if you have it. we test cold-start by restarting runtimes and measuring ramp. dedicated removes noisy neighbors but you still need to tune batch sizes.
[06:58] Priya: success criteria checklist recap: p95 < 1.2s for 50 conc; error rate < 0.5%; no >2% quality regression vs baseline; cost per 1k requests within x band. is that accurate?
[07:12] Sofia: yes that's the core. add: model variant compatibility and streaming latency for first token under 400ms for interactive flows.
[07:22] Marisol: we also want a clear handoff doc for our infra team, a runbook for failover (fallback to smaller model) and a simple cost estimation calc post-run.
[07:35] Evan: will do. we'll include a runbook + cost calc spreadsheet.
[07:40] James: any concerns around rate limits on your hosted endpoints during load tests?
[07:45] Sofia: we'll whitelist your test IP and provision a higher quota for test windows. if running in Redwood Private inside your VPC that won't be necessary.
[07:57] Priya: you mentioned regression alerts — are those part of Redwood Optimize or separate?
[08:02] Evan: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring tied to eval sets and can send alerts if diffs exceed a threshold. for the POC we'll enable a basic alerting policy and send weekly summaries or immediate alerts for big regressions.
[08:17] Marisol: for the harness — is there an example config for our exact case? long seqs, single-turn summarization, 50 concurrency?
[08:26] Evan: yes there's an example in the repo under examples/clinical_summarization.yaml — it has fields for sequence distribution, concurrency, and tokenization shim. Sofia will link it.
[08:38] Sofia: i'll drop links after the call. i'll also attach the SOC2 + security whitepaper and the quickstart.
[08:45] James: about metrics export — can we ship Prometheus metrics or do you only provide Grafana snapshots?
[08:52] Evan: harness exposes Prometheus; in hosted mode we can push to a Redwood-managed metrics endpoint, or you can scrape from your VPC. we'll provide a Grafana dashboard template.
[09:05] Marisol: concerning model quantization — we might need to test 4-bit and nf4. have you seen quality impacts on clinical text?
[09:15] Evan: yes quantization sometimes affects subtle tokenization boundaries; that's why we include A/B per-prompt diffs. often 4-bit is fine for many summarization workloads but we track exact eval metrics so you can decide.
[09:30] Priya: let's talk about success criteria instrumentation — we want automated per-prompt ROUGE and a simple pass/fail threshold per prompt. can your system do that in the POC?
[09:40] Evan: yep, we can run your eval harness as part of the post-processing step and emit a pass/fail column per request in the CSV. we can also track aggregated percent below threshold.
[09:52] James: for the load schedule — we need a 3-hour window. can you recommend the best time so it doesn't hit our peak internal traffic?
[09:59] Sofia: usually late weekend or a weekday night is best; propose Saturday 2025-03-29 02:00–05:00 UTC. we'll coordinate maintenance windows with your infra.
[10:15] Marisol: that works in principle — i'll confirm with ops.
[10:22] Evan: odd corner cases to note — if your pre/post-processing is GPU-accelerated on your side that may alter latency numbers; try to run identical pipeline as production for accurate results.
[10:36] Marisol: noted.
[10:40] Sofia: quick follow-on: we'll create a collaborative doc with the test matrix and expected metrics; will share by 2025-03-14.
[10:50] James: for the harness credentials flow, can you support short-lived tokens? we prefer ephemeral creds.
[10:56] Evan: yes, short-lived tokens via our auth layer or you can use your KMS-signed tokens if running from your VPC.
[11:05] Priya: any red flags from your side for this POC?
[11:09] Evan: only that we need representative payloads and the eval harness early; without those the numbers will be noisy. also worth noting streaming and non-streaming results can diverge — pick the mode that reflects your expected production traffic.
[11:26] Marisol: we'll prioritize uploading payloads.
[11:30] Sofia: ok, wrapping up. Recap of agreed items and owners: 1) Redwood share harness repo + example configs (Sofia) 2) Aurora upload sample payloads to S3 (James) 3) SE to prepare test matrix and streaming vs non-streaming plan (Evan) 4) schedule 3-hour load window week of 2025-03-24 (Sofia + Aur ops)
[11:55] Priya: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[12:00] Sofia: thanks all — we'll follow up with the links and the matrix.

End of transcript.
